Lawn watering can account for 50% to 90% of household water usage in urban areas, as stated by Survis and Root (2016). Watering lawns during peak daytime hours not only wastes water but also increases the risk of disease due to excessive evaporation (Survis and Root, 2016). With water demand expected to rise by 40% by 2050 and water shortages projected to affect more than half of the world's population by 2025, addressing this issue has become crucial (Eliasson, 2015).


I strongly recommend that you introduce an enforceable bylaw that prohibits grass watering between the hours of 8 a.m. and 11 p.m. To support enforcement of this bylaw, the city should consider hiring additional bylaw officers to patrol the city, address complaints about violations, and ensure compliance.
